To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-phenyl-piperazine heterocycle derivatives were designed, synthesized, and pharmacologically evaluated as multi-target compounds for the treatment of schizophrenic symptoms.
the isosteric replacement at the heterocyclic position of the N-phenyl-piperazine biaryl scaffold generated compounds with an adequate binding profile for D(2) and 5-HT receptors.

N-phenyl-piperazine derivatives with a 2-methyl-imidazo[1,2-α]pyridine moiety are multi-target antipsychoactive agents that are orally active and have a potential for the treatment of positive symptoms in schizophrenia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel heterocyclic N-(4-phenylp-1-piperazinyl) derivatives with a dual action on dopamine and serotonin receptors as potential antipsychotics.
the design and synthesis of new multi-target ligands for the treatment of psychotic disorders.
the development of novel heterocyclic N-piperazine derivatives as a new class of multi-target antipsycotic drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these new compounds represent a novel class of multi-target compounds that could be useful for the treatment and prevention of schizophrenia.
the 2-methyl-1H-imidazole[1, 2-a]pyrazine-8-carboxamide derivatives are promising multi-target ligands for schizophrenia treatment.
the N-phenyl heterocyclic derivatives described herein may represent a new class of multi-target antipsycotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the replacement of the biaryl heteroatom with a pyrazole, a triazole, and an imidazole ring, respectively, resulted in a series of N-phenypiperazine derivatives that are potent and selective ligands for dopamine D(2)- and 5-HT-1A receptors.
the N-phenyl-piperazine derivatives with a heterocyclic moiety in position 2 are promising candidates for the treatment of schizophrenic symptoms.
the N-phenylpyrazole derivatives are promising candidates for the development of multi-target antipsyhotic drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 2-methyl-1H-imidazo[1,2-α]pyridine-3-yl moiety is an excellent scaffold for the design of multi-target ligands with high affinity for dopamine receptors and moderate affinity for 5-HT( 1A) receptors.

the replacement of the heteroaryl ring in N-phenyl-piperazine ligands for D(2) and 5-HT receptors by pyrazole and imidazo[1,2-b]pyridine resulted in a new series of multi-target compounds with improved pharmacological profile.
a small structural modification at the heterocyclic moiety can be used as a tool for the design of multi-target ligands with potential for the treatment of positive symptoms of schizophrenia.
